newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile postpones April 7 cobalt sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile postpones April 7 cobalt sale.

text.p: The Defense National Stockpile Center said it has postponed its April 7 offer of 1 million pounds of cobalt until further notice following a court hearing on Thursday.

The judge in the U.S. Federal Claims Court asked for the April 7 offer to be delayed because he wanted more information from the Stockpile before ruling on whether to grant a temporary restraining order sought by Minor Metals, Inc, a cobalt trading company, a stockpile official said.
It was unclear how much time it would take to provide the information or when the sale could proceed, he added.
The April 7 sealed bid had already been postponed from March 31 in order to hear the Minor Metals complaint.
The Stockpile is scheduled to make a negotiated sale of cobalt sometime this month, with another sealed bid offer in May.
The resumption of sealed bid offers could take weeks rather than days, the stockpile official said, but stressed the situation should be clearer by next week.
It is thought that Minor Metals had objected to the sealed bid sale process because of a ruling that bidders were not allowed to make "all or nothing" offers.
The Stockpile prefers to have the freedom to award only some items to any bidder.
Minor Metals also complained to the General Accounting Office regarding the negotiated bid offer that was concluded late March.
The company accused the Stockpile of potentially revealing sensitive information about Minor Metals to other bidders - a charge strenuously denied by Stockpile officials.
